sources.title: Trello vs Jira 2026: 38% Price Gap and 3,000 vs 200 Integrations
sources.content: Event planning, editorial calendars, product launches, and personal project management all benefit from Trello’s low overhead. As MKBHD has discussed when reviewing productivity tools, the tool you actually use is better than the theoretically superior tool collecting dust. Trello’s adoption rate among non-technical teams reflects this principle. With over 50 million users worldwide, Trello’s user base dwarfs most competing visual project management tools because the barrier to entry is nearly zero — though it’s worth noting that within the narrower project-management software category specifically, 6sense data cited by Planyway put Trello at just a 0.47% market share as of January 2026, a reminder that raw user counts and category share measure different things. [...] Trello offers over 200 Power-Ups in its directory. Key integrations include Slack, Google Drive, Dropbox, GitHub, Salesforce, and Microsoft Teams. Trello’s free plan allows one Power-Up per board, while Standard and above allow unlimited Power-Ups. The Power-Up system is straightforward: find an integration, click enable, authorize the connection, and it appears on your board. Popular Power-Ups include calendar views, card repeater, voting, and time tracking, and Trello’s March 2026 changelog added a new card buttons menu that surfaces Power-Up actions directly from the card view for faster access. [...] In 2026, Trello Premium offers six views: Board, Timeline (Gantt-style), Calendar, Dashboard, Map, and Table. Jira provides Board, List, Timeline, Calendar, and Backlog views, plus advanced roadmaps in Premium that let you plan across multiple teams and projects. Jira’s roadmap feature alone is a reason many organizations choose it over Trello for cross-team planning.
